slides.title: Percent problems: where ^^obvious answers^^ go to die
slides.badge: The trap is always one of the choices

slides.title: Up 20%, down 20% ≠ even
slides.body: The second 20% is taken from a *bigger* number, so it removes more than the first 20% added. You end at $96 — down 4%, not back to even.

slides.stem: A shirt costs $80 after a 20% discount. What was the original price?
slides.prompt: Most students pick the same wrong answer. Comment yours.

slides.title: B — $100
slides.body: $96 is the bait — it takes 20% of the *sale* price. To undo a 20% discount, divide by 0.8. The discount came off the original, not off $80.
